learn.hook: The bangle stall has a huge heap. Guess first: 100? 200? 300?
points: First guess how many, then count to check your guess.
Count big heaps in groups of 10: 10, 20, 30 ... It is quicker and you do not lose track.
250 is 200 and 50 more. 280 is 200 and 80 more.
To find how many more make 300, count on from the number: 260 + 40 = 300.
To find which heap is more, compare the numbers: 270 is more than 250.

example.q: A stall has 260 balloons. How many more are needed to make 300?

learn.reallife: At a fair, ticket sellers count notes in bundles of 10 to be quick and correct.

quiz.q: A heap of bangles is counted in groups of 10. There are 24 groups. How many bangles?
Raju guessed 200 marbles. He counted 230. How far off was he?
Which shows 250?
A stall has 275 kites. How many more to make 300?
Stall A has 268 toys. Stall B has 286. Which has more?
quiz.explain: Both have 2 hundreds. 8 tens is more than 6 tens, so 286 is more.

quiz.q: Why do we count a big heap in groups of 10?
options: It is quicker and easier to keep track
quiz.explain: Groups of 10 can be counted 10, 20, 30, so we do not lose count.

quiz.q: Meena counted 20 groups of 10 and 7 more. How many?
A stall had 300 balloons. 40 flew away. How many are left?

teach.ask: Gappu sees a big pile of seeds at the mela. How can he count them without losing track?
teach.praise: Guess first, then count in tens: 10, 20, 30... Chirp!
teach.nudge: How can I group the seeds to count faster?

learn.hook: A cinema hall can have hundreds of seats! Let's learn to read and write such big numbers.
points: We can count in hundreds: 100, 200, 300 ... up to 900.
A 3-digit number has a hundreds digit, a tens digit and a ones digit.
We read 457 as 'four hundred fifty-seven'.
The smallest 3-digit number is 100 and the largest is 999.
After 999 comes 1000, our first 4-digit number.

steps: No tens, so the tens digit is 0

learn.reallife: Bus numbers, house numbers and the price of a school bag often have 3 digits.

items.text: Eight hundred twenty in numbers is ___.

quiz.q: Count in hundreds: 200, 300, 400, ___
Write 'five hundred thirty-six' in numbers.
quiz.explain: Five hundred is 500, thirty is 30 and six is 6. 500 + 30 + 6 = 536.
quiz.mistake: Writes 500 and then 36 next to it

quiz.q: Write 'seven hundred four' in numbers.
quiz.explain: 7 hundreds, no tens and 4 ones. The 0 holds the tens place: 704.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 0 in the tens place

quiz.q: What number comes just after 599?
quiz.explain: 1 more than 599 is 600. The 9 ones and 9 tens roll over into one more hundred.
quiz.mistake: Writes 5 and then 100 next to it

quiz.q: Which is the largest 3-digit number?
quiz.explain: 999 has the biggest digit, 9, in every place. 1000 has 4 digits.

quiz.q: How do you read 860?
quiz.explain: 860 is 8 hundreds and 6 tens, so we say eight hundred sixty.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the 0 or reads the digits in the wrong places

quiz.q: A cinema has 300 seats downstairs and 200 seats upstairs. How many seats are there in all?
Count back in hundreds: 900, 800, 700, ___

teach.ask: Gappu sees 'five hundred forty-two' on a bus. How should he write it in numbers?
teach.praise: 542! Five hundreds, four tens and two ones. I can read buses now!
teach.nudge: Which digit goes first, and what does 'forty' become?

learn.hook: 347 can be 300 + 47, or 340 + 7, or 3 hundreds 4 tens 7 ones. How many ways can you find?
points: Fill missing numbers on a path by finding the step: 312, 313, ___, 315.
Matchstick bundles show numbers: big bundles of 100, small bundles of 10, and loose sticks.
One number can be written in many number sentences: 365 = 300 + 65 = 360 + 5 = 300 + 60 + 5.
To write the number in a picture, count the hundreds, then tens, then ones.

example.q: A picture shows 3 big bundles, 2 small bundles and 6 loose sticks. What number is it?

learn.reallife: A cashier may count ₹347 as three ₹100 notes, four ₹10 notes and seven ₹1 coins.

quiz.q: Which number is missing? 356, 357, ___, 359
3 bundles of 100, 0 bundles of 10 and 8 sticks show which number?
Which number sentence equals 365?
What is 200 + 150?
Which is NOT another way to write 284?
A picture shows 2 hundred-bundles, 13 ten-bundles and 0 loose sticks. What number?
quiz.mistake: Writes the counts side by side

quiz.q: Continue the path: 340, 350, 360, ___

teach.ask: Gappu wants to write 246 in two different ways. Can you help him?
teach.nudge: Can I split 246 at the hundreds?

topics.title: Number slider and guess my number

learn.hook: Slide 1 more, 10 more, 20 less... Watch which digit changes!
points: Add or take away 1: only the ones digit changes (unless it crosses a ten). 245 + 1 = 246.
Add or take away 10: the tens digit changes. 245 + 10 = 255.
Adding 20 changes the tens digit by 2: 245 + 20 = 265.
In 'guess my number', use clues like 'more than' and 'less than' to narrow down the range.
Each good guess cuts the range: if it is between 200 and 300 and more than 250, try 275.

example.q: Start at 318. Add 2, then take away 10.

learn.reallife: Lift buttons and TV channel buttons go up and down by 1. Number sliders work the same way.

games.title: Which digit changes?
items: Adding 10 to 342 changes the tens digit.
Adding 1 to 342 changes the hundreds digit.

quiz.q: What is 237 + 10?
quiz.explain: Adding 10 makes the tens digit go up by 1.

quiz.q: What is 452 − 2?
Which digit changes when you add 10 to 364?
What is 196 + 20?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry into the hundreds

quiz.q: Guess my number: it is between 300 and 400. It is more than 350. It is less than 360. It ends in 5. What is it?
Guess my number: it is 10 less than 250. What is it?
Riya's guess is 200. Clue: 'More!' Her next guess is 300. Clue: 'Less!' What does she know?
quiz.explain: More than 200 and less than 300, so between them.

quiz.q: What is 300 − 1?

teach.ask: Gappu adds 10 to 426 and gets 427. What went wrong?
teach.praise: Adding 10 changes the tens, so 426 + 10 = 436! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Which digit should change when I add 10?

learn.hook: Pick any number, count the letters in its name, and keep going. You will always reach FOUR! Try it!
points: Magical count: write a number name, count its letters, and use that count as the next number.
Example: 23 → twenty-three (11 letters) → eleven (6) → six (3) → three (5) → five (4) → four (4).
FOUR has 4 letters, so the chain stops there.
The next hundred after a number is the first hundred bigger than it: after 347 comes 400.
We can show it on a number line or with bundles: 347 needs 3 more sticks to make 350, then 50 more to make 400. That is 53 in all.
learn.reallife: Number-name games help you spell numbers correctly for cheques and forms.

quiz.q: How many letters are in 'fifteen'?
Magical count for 15: fifteen → 7 → ? What comes next?
quiz.explain: seven has 5 letters, so the next number is 5.
quiz.mistake: Counts the letters of fifteen again

quiz.q: Where does every magical count end?
quiz.explain: four has exactly 4 letters, so the chain stops at 4.

quiz.q: What is the next hundred after 438?
quiz.explain: 438 is between 400 and 500. The next hundred is 500.

quiz.q: How many more does 438 need to reach its next hundred?
Magical count for 40: forty → ?
What is the next hundred after 299?
Ravi has 3 bundles of 100 and 7 bundles of 10. How many more bundles of 10 make the next hundred?

teach.ask: Gappu picked 99 for the magical count. What happens?
teach.nudge: How many letters are in ninety-nine?

learn.hook: Where does 243 live on the number line? Between which neighbours?
points: To place 216 on a line, find 210 and 220, then go 6 steps past 210.
235 lies between 200 and 300. It is also between 200 and 250.
The distance to the next hundred: 387 → 390 is 3, 390 → 400 is 10. So 13.
Compare by jumping: 393 to 400 is a jump of 7, so 400 is 7 more than 393.
learn.reallife: Milestones on highways are like a number line: you can see how far the next town is.

games.title: How far to the next hundred?

quiz.q: Between which two tens does 243 lie?
quiz.explain: 243 is 3 more than 240 and 7 less than 250.
quiz.mistake: Picks the hundreds instead of the tens

quiz.q: 235 is between 200 and 300. Is it closer to 200 or to 250?
quiz.explain: 235 is 15 away from 250 but 35 away from 200.

quiz.q: How far is 387 from 400?
How much bigger is 400 than 393?
Which number is between 250 and 300?
quiz.explain: 257 is more than 250 and less than 300.

quiz.q: On a line from 210 to 220, where is 216?
Which hundred is 329 closer to, 300 or 400?
quiz.explain: 329 is 29 away from 300 but 71 away from 400.

quiz.q: Jump from 365 by 5, then by 30. Where do you land?

teach.ask: Gappu is at 376 on a number line and wants to fly to 400. How far must he go?
teach.praise: 376 to 380 is 4, 380 to 400 is 20, so 24! Chirp!
teach.nudge: What is the next ten after 376?

learn.hook: Farooq Chacha arranges barfis in neat rows. Counting is easy when the rows are equal!
points: Sweets in equal rows can be counted row by row: 5 rows of 10 is 50.
If a tray holds 100 and has 80, it needs 20 more to be full.
After filling, add to find the new total: 3 full trays of 100 and 1 tray of 60 is 360.
Numbers between 400 and 500 sit after 400 on the line: 450 is halfway, 480 is near 500.

example.q: A tray holds 100 laddoos in 10 rows of 10. It has 7 full rows. How many more to fill it?

learn.reallife: Sweet shops arrange sweets in rows on trays so that they can count stock quickly.

quiz.q: A tray has 8 rows of 10 jalebis. How many jalebis?
A tray holds 100 barfis. It has 64. How many more fill it?
Farooq Chacha has 4 full trays of 100 and fills another tray with 25. How many sweets in all?
Which number is halfway between 400 and 500?
quiz.explain: 450 is 50 more than 400 and 50 less than 500.

quiz.q: Is 480 closer to 400 or 500?
quiz.explain: 480 is 20 away from 500 and 80 away from 400.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the hundreds digit

quiz.q: A tray has 3 rows of 10 and 4 more. How many sweets?
A tray had 90 sweets. 10 more were added. Now 2 full trays of 100 and this tray. Total?
Which number lies between 430 and 440?
quiz.explain: 436 is more than 430 and less than 440.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number with the right digits in the wrong places

teach.ask: Gappu has a tray of 100 places and 72 seeds in it. How many more fill the tray?
teach.praise: 72 to 80 is 8, 80 to 100 is 20, so 28! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How far is 72 from the next ten?

learn.hook: In this building, the house numbers follow a secret pattern. Can you crack it?
points: In our building, each row (floor) has 10 houses. House numbers go up by 1 to the right.
Going up one floor adds 10. Going down one floor takes away 10.
So moving left or right changes the ones digit, and moving up or down changes the tens digit.
To find a house, look at its tens to find the floor row and its ones to find the column.
'Who am I?' riddles use clues about digits and places.

example.q: The ground row has 301 to 310. House 324 is how many floors up, and in which column?
steps: 324 is the 4th house in that row

learn.reallife: Hotel rooms are often numbered so the first digits tell the floor and the last digits tell the room.

quiz.q: In the building, floors go up by 10. What house is directly above 342?
Which house is to the right of 358?
Moving down one floor from 375 gives which house?
When you move left or right in this building, which digit changes?
quiz.explain: Left and right are steps of 1.

quiz.mistake: Looks only at the ones digit

quiz.q: Who am I? I am 2 floors above 314.
Who am I? My hundreds digit is 3, my tens digit is 1 more than 3, my ones digit is 0.
quiz.mistake: Puts the digits in the wrong places

quiz.q: House numbers in a column: 305, 315, 325, ___. What comes next?

teach.ask: Gappu lives in house 347. His friend lives one floor up, one house to the right. Which house is that?
teach.nudge: What changes when I go up one floor?

learn.hook: 275 laddoos to pack. Big boxes hold 100, small boxes hold 10. How many of each?
points: Pack the biggest boxes first: 275 = 2 boxes of 100, 7 boxes of 10 and 5 loose.
10 tens make 1 hundred. If we open a box of 100, we get 10 boxes of 10.
So 2 hundreds = 20 tens, and 3 hundreds 4 tens = 34 tens.
Numbers from 200 to 300 that have a 5: 205, 215, ... and all of 250 to 259. There are 19.
Show and tell: one child asks 'How many tens in 340?' and the next answers and asks a new question.

example.q: Pack 342 sweets. How many boxes of 100, boxes of 10 and loose sweets?

learn.reallife: Bakeries pack biscuits in packets of 10 and cartons of 100 so they can count stock quickly.

quiz.q: How many boxes of 100 are needed to pack 438 sweets (with tens and loose)?
How many tens are there in 1 hundred?
Open 3 boxes of 100. How many boxes of 10 do you get?
How many tens are there in 250 altogether?
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the tens digit

quiz.q: Which number between 200 and 300 does NOT have a 5?
quiz.mistake: Misses the 5 in the tens place

quiz.q: How many numbers from 250 to 259 are there?
How many numbers between 200 and 300 contain the digit 5?
Show and tell: 'I have 5 boxes of 100, 0 boxes of 10 and 6 loose.' What is the number?

teach.ask: Gappu opened a box of 100 seeds. He found smaller packets of 10 inside. How many packets?
teach.nudge: How many tens make one hundred?

learn.hook: Every digit lives in its own house: Hundreds House, Tens House or Ones House!
points: In 358, the 3 is in the hundreds place, the 5 is in the tens place and the 8 is in the ones place.
358 = 300 + 50 + 8. This is called the expanded form.
The same digit has a different value in a different place. In 535, the first 5 is worth 500 and the last 5 is worth 5.
Zero keeps a place empty: 405 has 0 tens.
learn.reallife: ₹100 notes, ₹10 notes and ₹1 coins work just like hundreds, tens and ones.

quiz.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in 739?
quiz.explain: 7 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 7 hundreds = 700.
quiz.mistake: Gives the digit instead of its value

quiz.q: Which is the expanded form of 481?
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits without their place values

quiz.q: 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones make which number?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the 0 in the tens place

quiz.q: Harpreet has three ₹100 notes, two ₹10 notes and six ₹1 coins. How much money does she have?
quiz.mistake: Counts the notes and coins instead of their values

quiz.q: In 555, what is the value of the 5 in the tens place?
quiz.explain: A 5 in the tens place means 5 tens = 50.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every 5 in 555 has the same value

quiz.q: How many hundreds are there in 800?
Which number has 6 in the ones place?
quiz.explain: The ones place is the last digit. Only 406 ends in 6.
quiz.mistake: Looks for 6 in any place, not just the ones place

quiz.q: What number is 600 + 5 + 30?
quiz.explain: 600 is 6 hundreds, 30 is 3 tens and 5 is 5 ones. Put them in their places: 635.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits in the order they are given, not by place

teach.ask: Gappu thinks both 5s in 535 are worth the same. Is he right? Explain to him.
teach.praise: One 5 is 500 and the other is just 5! The place decides the value!
teach.nudge: Where is each 5 sitting? Does that change what it is worth?

learn.hook: Two trains, 845 and 854 passengers. Which one is more crowded? Let's find out!
points: To compare, look at the hundreds first: 512 > 498 because 5 hundreds is more than 4 hundreds.
If the hundreds are the same, compare the tens. If the tens are also the same, compare the ones.
> means 'greater than' and < means 'less than'. The open side faces the bigger number.
100 more than 345 is 445. 10 less than 345 is 335.

example.q: Arrange 607, 670 and 760 from smallest to biggest.
steps: 607 and 670 both have 6 hundreds. Tens: 0 and 7.

learn.reallife: Comparing prices helps you pick the cheaper cycle, and comparing scores tells you which team won.

games.title: Bigger or smaller?
items: Both have 6 hundreds. 3 tens is more than 0 tens, so 630 > 603.
The hundreds digit goes up by 1: 245 + 100 = 345.
Both have 9 hundreds. 0 tens is less than 9 tens, so 909 < 990.
Same digits in the same places make equal numbers.

quiz.q: Which is greater: 512 or 498?
quiz.explain: Compare hundreds first. 5 hundreds is more than 4 hundreds, so 512 is greater.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the 9s in 498 and thinks it is bigger

quiz.q: Which sign makes this true? 630 ___ 603
quiz.explain: Same hundreds. 3 tens is more than 0 tens, so 630 > 603.

quiz.q: What is 100 more than 456?
quiz.explain: 100 more adds 1 to the hundreds digit: 456 + 100 = 556.

quiz.q: What is 10 less than 382?
quiz.explain: 10 less takes 1 away from the tens digit: 382 − 10 = 372.

quiz.q: Which is the smallest: 415, 451, 514 or 541?
quiz.explain: 415 and 451 have the fewest hundreds (4). Between them, 1 ten is less than 5 tens, so 415 is smallest.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the last digit

quiz.q: The Delhi train has 845 passengers and the Mumbai train has 854. Which train has more passengers?
quiz.explain: Both have 8 hundreds. 5 tens is more than 4 tens, so 854 is more.

quiz.q: Which list goes from smallest to biggest?
quiz.explain: 230 has 2 hundreds, so it is smallest. 302 has 0 tens and 320 has 2 tens, so 302 comes before 320.
quiz.mistake: Thinks numbers with the same digits are all equal

quiz.q: Using the digits 4, 7 and 2 once each, what is the biggest number you can make?
quiz.explain: Put the biggest digit in the hundreds place, the next in tens, the smallest in ones: 742.
quiz.mistake: Puts the biggest digit in the ones place

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 609 is bigger than 690 because 9 is a big digit. Help him compare!
teach.praise: Same hundreds, so I check the tens! 690 is bigger. Thank you!
teach.nudge: Which place should I look at after the hundreds?

learn.hook: To compare 452 and 458, do you need to look at the hundreds? No! Find the place that decides.
points: To compare, look from the left. The first place where the digits differ decides.
452 and 458: hundreds same, tens same, ones differ. The ones place decides.
317 and 371: hundreds same, tens differ. The tens place decides.
With digits 1, 2 and 3 (no repeating), we can make 6 numbers: 123, 132, 213, 231, 312, 321.
If digits can repeat, we can make more numbers, like 111, 112 and 333.

example.q: Make all 3-digit numbers with 4, 5 and 6, using each digit once.

learn.reallife: Bus numbers, house numbers and locker codes are made by arranging digits.

quiz.q: Comparing 645 and 649, which place decides?
quiz.explain: Hundreds same, tens same, ones 5 and 9 differ.

quiz.q: Comparing 382 and 328, which place decides?
Comparing 719 and 791, which is bigger?
quiz.explain: Tens decide: 9 tens is more than 1 ten.

quiz.q: How many 3-digit numbers can be made with 2, 5 and 8, using each once?
Using 3, 0 and 6 once each, which order does NOT give a 3-digit number?
quiz.explain: Starting with 0 gives 036, which is just 36, a 2-digit number.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a leading zero is fine

quiz.q: Using 4 and 7, with repeats allowed, how many 2-digit numbers can you make?
Using 1, 5 and 9 once each, what is the smallest number?
Using digits 3 and 8 with repeats, which is the biggest 3-digit number?
quiz.explain: Repeats allowed, so use 8 in every place.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to compare 527 and 572. Does he need to check the hundreds or the tens?
teach.praise: Hundreds are the same, the tens decide: 572 is bigger! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Which place is the first one that is different?
